dedupe_keys.name: electrical japan power plant map and database of about 6 000 japanese power stations with demand visualisation

description: Electrical Japan is a web site built after the 2011 Great East Japan Earthquake to consider Japan's power problems by visualising supply through a power plant map and consumption through a night-light map. Its own power plant database, collected one plant at a time from public web and book sources and mapped by hand, holds about 6,000 plants, which the site describes as not open data. Maps and searches cover thermal, biomass, nuclear, hydro, pumped storage, geothermal, wind, solar and battery storage sites, by company, type, output, name and prefecture. The site also presents electricity use, solar and wind output, supply and demand by source, renewable curtailment, feed-in tariff data and records of large blackouts, and overlays plants with landslide and flood inundation risk. A page on open data compares this database with the government National Land Numerical Information power facilities data (more than 12,000 entries, 2013 edition) and an EIA-based US version, and explains gaps in the government data such as missing mid-sized hydro and feed-in tariff solar plants. Coverage is Japan. Viewing is free; the plant data are not released under an open licence. Caveats: it is compiled by one author, and reuse terms are not stated. Simulation uses are plant locations and capacity for exposure of generation to landslides and floods and for supply studies. Related records: data-japan-ksj-power-generation-facilities-p03 is the government data set.
